zh-CN: 白桦：面向开发者的开放式协作网络
en-US: Baihua: An Open Collaboration Network for Developers

zh-CN:
白桦（Baihua）的愿景，是成为一款以开发者为中心、尊重隐私、由不同团队共同参与的联邦式协作应用。它希望把开发工作中彼此分散的沟通与工具连接起来，让人们能够围绕项目协作，同时保留对自己的数据、服务和工作方式的掌控。白桦也希望支持自由表达与自由协作：让不同观点能够被分享，让个人和团队可以自愿选择合作方式、工具与伙伴。

今天的开发工作常常穿梭于终端、代码托管平台、问题跟踪工具、构建系统和聊天软件之间。信息散落在不同平台，协作也被切成许多互不相连的步骤。白桦希望逐步减少这种割裂：让交流、代码、任务和自动化能力围绕同一个项目上下文协同，让开发者少在工具之间来回切换，把更多精力留给真正的创造和解决问题。开放而可互通的协作，也能降低对单一平台的依赖，让参与者更自由地迁移、选择和共同建设。

## 一个由许多社区组成的协作网络

白桦所说的联邦式协作，是让不同团队和社区能够各自运行白桦服务，同时在彼此认可的边界内建立联系、交换协作信息。每个组织可以选择自己的服务提供者，也可以自行托管；用户和团队不必把所有沟通与数据都交给同一个中心化平台。

这样的网络既要让跨团队协作成为可能，也要尊重各个参与方的自主权。服务管理者可以决定谁能加入、哪些内容可以共享、如何管理数据以及与哪些其他服务建立连接。用户则可以在清晰的授权和可理解的规则下参与协作。白桦希望不同服务之间能够互通，而不是要求所有人都迁入同一个平台。人们可以围绕共同兴趣、项目和目标自由结成协作关系；表达观点、分享成果和开展合作，不必以服从单一服务提供者的规则为前提。

## 让开发工具围绕项目协同

白桦不只想成为开发者聊天的地方，也希望成为连接日常开发工作的协作空间。围绕一个项目，团队可以交流想法、跟进问题、分享文件，并逐步把代码变更、讨论和任务进展放进同一条协作脉络中。

Git 是这条愿景中的重要组成部分。白桦希望让本地工作目录与远程仓库更自然地协同：开发者可以在熟悉的本地环境工作，也能在协作空间中理解远程代码的变化、讨论提交与分支、衔接团队的审阅和交付流程。目标是让本地开发与团队协作彼此连贯，而不是把开发者锁进单一托管平台或强迫他们放弃现有工作方式。

插件化是扩展这类协作能力的重要方向。不同团队使用的语言、工具链和工作流程并不相同，因此白桦希望提供清晰的扩展方式，让社区和团队能够按需接入开发工具、自动化任务和自定义协作流程。插件应当帮助用户组合适合自己的工作环境，同时让权限、数据访问范围和运行行为保持明确、可管理。

## 把隐私作为协作的基础

白桦希望让隐私成为贯穿产品设计的原则，而不是某个单独开关。用户应当清楚数据由谁保管、哪些参与者能够访问、服务之间交换了什么，以及如何撤回授权或离开一个协作空间。自主托管、开放协议和可审阅的实现，都是帮助个人与组织获得更多控制权的途径。自由表达与隐私彼此支撑：当人们能够理解信息如何被处理，并能自主选择分享范围，就更有条件安心地交流、探索想法和开展合作。

端到端加密是这一愿景的重要部分。白桦计划持续完善加密能力，让用户能够保护一对一交流、群组讨论以及协作过程中产生的敏感内容。加密应尽量减少服务提供者读取私密内容的机会，同时通过可信的身份验证和密钥管理，帮助参与者确认自己正在与谁交流。保护范围、使用方式和必要元数据都应当清楚说明，避免让用户误以为某种保护覆盖了实际上未受保护的内容。

隐私也需要与开放协作共存。白桦希望通过细致的授权、可见的共享边界和可扩展的集成方式，让团队在获得实用工具的同时决定哪些内容可以流转。插件、远程仓库和联邦连接都应遵循用户和组织设定的权限，而不应悄悄扩大数据访问范围。

## 由社区共同塑造

白桦的长期目标不是复制某一个现有平台，而是探索一种更开放的开发者协作方式：服务可以由不同的人运行，工具可以由社区扩展，团队可以按自己的需要组织工作，用户仍能理解并掌控自己的数据。

这是一条持续建设的道路。联邦互通、Git 本地与远程协同、插件生态，以及面向更多协作场景的加密保护，都是白桦希望逐步实现的方向。白桦欢迎开发者、团队和社区参与讨论与建设，一起把分散的开发工具连接起来，让协作更连贯，也让隐私和自主权始终留在设计的中心。
en-US:
Baihua envisions becoming a developer-centered, privacy-respecting, federated collaboration application built with the participation of many teams. It aims to connect the communication and tools that are scattered across development work, helping people collaborate around projects while keeping control of their data, services, and ways of working. Baihua also aims to support freedom of expression and freedom to collaborate: people should be able to share different perspectives and choose how, with whom, and through which tools they work together.

Today, development work often moves between a terminal, code hosting services, issue tracking tools, build systems, and chat applications. Information is scattered across platforms, and collaboration is divided into disconnected steps. Baihua hopes to gradually reduce this fragmentation by bringing communication, code, tasks, and automation together around a shared project context. Developers should spend less time switching tools and more time creating and solving problems. Open and interoperable collaboration can also reduce dependence on any single platform, giving participants more freedom to move, choose, and build together.

## A collaboration network made up of many communities

By federated collaboration, Baihua means enabling different teams and communities to run their own Baihua services while connecting and exchanging collaboration information within boundaries they agree upon. Each organization can choose a service provider or host its own service. Users and teams do not have to entrust all of their communication and data to one centralized platform.

This network should make collaboration across teams possible while respecting the autonomy of each participant. Service operators can decide who may join, what can be shared, how data is managed, and which other services to connect with. Users should be able to take part under clear permissions and understandable rules. Baihua aims to let different services interoperate without requiring everyone to move to the same platform. People can form working relationships around shared interests, projects, and goals. Expressing ideas, sharing work, and collaborating should not require submitting to the rules of a single service provider.

## Development tools working together around projects

Baihua aims to be more than a place for developers to chat. It wants to become a collaboration space that connects the work of software development. Around a project, a team should be able to exchange ideas, track issues, share files, and gradually bring code changes, discussions, and task progress into one coherent thread of collaboration.

Git is an important part of this vision. Baihua hopes to make local working directories and remote repositories work together more naturally. Developers should be able to keep working in familiar local environments while understanding remote code changes in their collaboration space, discussing commits and branches, and connecting those discussions to review and delivery. The goal is to make local development and team collaboration feel continuous, without locking developers into one hosting service or forcing them to abandon their existing ways of working.

Plugins are an important way to extend these capabilities. Teams use different languages, toolchains, and workflows, so Baihua hopes to provide clear extension points through which communities and teams can connect development tools, automated tasks, and custom collaboration processes as needed. Plugins should help users assemble an environment that suits their work, while keeping permissions, data access, and runtime behavior clear and manageable.

## Privacy as the foundation of collaboration

Baihua aims to make privacy a principle that runs through product design, rather than a single setting. Users should be able to understand who holds their data, which participants can access it, what services exchange, and how to withdraw permission or leave a collaborative space. Self-hosting, open protocols, and implementations that can be inspected are ways to give individuals and organizations greater control. Freedom of expression and privacy reinforce one another: when people understand how information is handled and can choose the scope of sharing, they have more room to communicate, explore ideas, and work together with confidence.

End-to-end encryption is an important part of this vision. Baihua plans to continue improving encryption so that users can protect one-to-one conversations, group discussions, and sensitive content created during collaboration. Encryption should reduce service providers' ability to read private content as much as possible. Trustworthy identity verification and key management should also help participants confirm whom they are communicating with. The scope and use of protection, along with necessary metadata, should be explained clearly so users are not led to believe that content is protected when it is not.

Privacy must also coexist with open collaboration. Baihua hopes to give teams detailed permissions, visible sharing boundaries, and extensible integrations, so they can decide what information may flow while using practical tools. Plugins, remote repositories, and federated connections should follow the permissions set by users and organizations; they should never silently expand access to data.

## Shaped together with the community

Baihua's long-term goal is not to copy any one existing platform. It is to explore a more open way for developers to collaborate: services can be run by different people, tools can be extended by the community, teams can organize their work as they choose, and users can continue to understand and control their data.

This is a path of continuous development. Federation between services, collaboration between local and remote Git work, a plugin ecosystem, and encryption for a broader range of collaborative settings are all directions Baihua hopes to pursue over time. Baihua welcomes developers, teams, and communities to take part in discussion and development. Together, we can connect scattered development tools, make collaboration more coherent, and keep privacy and autonomy at the center of the design.
